ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the area of $\triangle ABF$ is equal to that of the quadrilateral $CDFE$, with point $E$ on side $BC$, $AE\parallel CD$ intersecting $BD$ at point $F$, $CD=12$, $EF=9$. What is the length of $AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
$\because$ The area of $\triangle ABF$ is equal to the area of the quadrilateral $CDFE$,\\
$\therefore$ The area of $\triangle BEA$ is equal to the area of $\triangle BCD$,\\
$\because$ $AE\parallel CD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BEF\sim \triangle BCD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle BEF}}{S_{\triangle BCD}}=\left(\frac{EF}{CD}\right)^2$\\
$\because$ $CD=12$ and $EF=9$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle BEF}}{S_{\triangle BCD}}=\left(\frac{9}{12}\right)^2=\frac{9}{16}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle BEF}}{S_{\triangle BEA}}=\frac{9}{16}$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{EF}{EA}=\frac{9}{16}$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AF}{EF}=\frac{7}{9}$\\
$\therefore$ $AF=\frac{7}{9}EF=\frac{7}{9}\times 9 = \boxed{7}$.

Then reason: The problem statement gives AE ∥ CD, and CD=12, EF=9, and area(△ABF)=area(quadrilateral CDFE). Because △ABE can be divided into △ABF and △BEF, and △BCD can be divided into quadrilateral CDFE and △BEF, area(△ABE)=area(△BCD). Also because AE ∥ CD, and B, E, C are collinear, B, F, D are collinear, △BEF ∼ △BCD. Thus the linear ratio EF/CD=9/12=3/4, and the area ratio area(△BEF)/area(△BCD)=(3/4)^2=9/16. From area(△ABE)=area(△BCD), get area(△BEF)/area(△ABE)=9/16. For △BEF and △BEA with the same vertex B, and with bases EF and EA on the same straight line AE, area(△BEF)/area(△BEA)=EF/EA=9/16, so EA=16. Finally AF=EA-EF=16-9=7.
